prerequisites: A2 level of French according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Know and use a second language to obtain information and communicate ideas within the corresponding professional field.
Integrate into international work groups, and be able to work effectively with colleagues from other languages and cultures.
Acquire transversal knowledge that falls outside the regulated curriculum in this degree but may be useful in any professional field.
Understand instructions in class and tasks given by a teacher or lecturer.
Understand basic instructions and messages with some help (simple specific texts, ...).
Write simple texts on familiar or predictable topics.
Express opinions on abstract or cultural matters in a limited way or offer advice within a known area.
Find solutions to unforeseen situations using French.
Know intermediate-level grammatical structures of the French language.
Communicate in French orally and in writing.

syllabus_topics: Communication in everyday life. Narrating and understanding personal biographies. Expressing feelings, tastes, and needs.
Media: radio, television, Internet, and press.
Academic and professional environment (University, company internships, working life).
Introduction to the Mechatronics specialty in French language.
teaching_methods: Classroom and laboratory practices, language lab (participative model focusing on communication between students and between students and teacher, including theoretical concepts and grammatical, lexical, and pragmatic notions)
Group tutorials (for resolving doubts, learning difficulties, exchanging impressions, and individualized complements for level uniformity problems)
Other activities (video viewing, conference attendance, multimedia activities)
Autonomous student work (reading proposed materials, searching or elaborating information, writing texts, practical work, preparing activities)
Team work (tasks in French to develop negotiation, communication, social skills, tolerance of diversity)

assessment_methods.method: Oral presentation of a structured work (Ordinary Call)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, assessment is based on a portfolio (20%), an oral presentation (30%), and written tests (50%). For the extraordinary call, evaluation consists of a final written exam (70%) and a final oral exam (30%). The evaluation aims to verify the fulfillment of objectives and competencies and contribute to the progress of learning outcomes.
